Click the"Start" button to start the experiment.
We require, powdered naphthalene, liquid paraffin, capillary tube, porous plate, spatula, thermometer, thread, beaker, stirrer, iron stamp with clamp, wire gauze, tripod stand, Bunsen burner etc..
Take the capillary tube and seal one end of it by heating it over the Bunsen burner.
Using the spatula take some powdered naphthalene.
Put it on the porous plate to make a heap of powdered naphthalene on the porous plate.
Push the open end of the capillary tube into the heap.
Some powdered sample will enter into the capillary.
Tap the sealed end of the capillary tube gently on the porous plate.
Repeat the same process and fill the capillary tube up to 2 - 3 mm.
Repeat the same process and fill the capillary tube up to 2 - 3 mm.
Attach the capillary tube to the thermometer using the thread.
Take the beaker containing the paraffin liquid.
Place it on the wire gauze placed over the Bunsen burner and insert a stirrer in it.
Clamp the thermometer carrying capillary tube in the iron stand. Adjust the arranngement and immerse the capillary tube and thermometer in liquid paraffin bath.
Make sure that the thread is outside the liquid paraffin bath.
Heat the liquid paraffin bath slowly and stir the liquid with the stirrer.
By moving it up and down so that the temperature remains uniform throughout.
After sometime, the naphthalene in the capillary tube will start melting.
Note the temperature (t1) when naphthalene starts melting.
After some time, the naphthalene in the test tube has completely melted.
Note the temperature (t2) when the naphthalene has melted completely.
Calculate the melting point of naphthalene using the formula (t1 + t2)/2.
